source_snapshot.items: Boot Order - Set boot option to BIOS for all future-boot
source_snapshot.procedure: Verify two BIOS prerequisites; set `ipmitool chassis bootdev bios options=efiboot,persistent`; read boot parameter 5; reboot into BIOS twice; note automatic boot-flag clear at about 60 seconds +/-10%; recover with `bootdev none options=persistent`; source asks to clear logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Both boots enter BIOS, the setting is correct, and POST visually announces that persistent boot order is set.
source_snapshot.script: Private all-future-boot path; 10 attended and 30 machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; proposes protected-target-incomplete IPMI set/readback and recognizes visual BIOS/POST work, but exposes credentials and omits the timer conflict plus verified clear/normal-boot proof.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at CRITICAL risk; requires vendor persistent/auto-clear semantics, two separately observed boots, POST evidence and mandatory recovery.

old_problem: The test asks one persistent BIOS-setup override to survive two reboot boundaries and govern all future boots, yet the same Procedure says BMC automatically clears the boot flag after roughly 60 seconds. It does not say whether this timer applies to a distinct one-time flag, the persistent selector, or contradicts the requested lifecycle. Because the lifetime model determines write/readback timing, both reboot expectations and whether `bootdev none options=persistent` clears every relevant layer, no successful command or first BIOS entry can settle the source conflict.
disposition_reason: Retain Engineering Decision Pending and source conflict, but keep REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION instead of BLOCKED. The source purpose, hazardous mutation and complete coverage are identifiable; firmware/vendor clarification can bind the timer to the correct flag layer and confirm a supported clear/recovery path. A parameterized state machine can therefore preserve baseline -> persistent set -> readback -> reboot 1 -> reboot 2 -> explicit clear -> normal OS Ready without inventing semantics. Nothing may execute until the owner/vendor supplies the flag-lifetime mapping, exact POST oracle and independently usable clear/recovery contract.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1635, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, V2, historical V3.1 record, pending/conflict analyses and duplicate identity search were read. The actual next formal queue identity was reconstructed and directly opened in XLSX as Functionality row 1638 / Wistron-BMC-00909-V003 / 7049bc17971bc0ac.

Persistence cannot be proved by immediate readback. The selected state must remain authoritative across both separately observed reboot boundaries; each trial needs command/readback, reboot/POST timeline, BIOS-entry marker and proof that no BIOS setting was saved.

The 60-second note may describe a different one-time valid bit, automatic BMC behavior or an actual contradiction. Standards knowledge cannot identify this platform's layer without firmware/vendor documentation, so the review must not declare the note inapplicable or rewrite it.

Recovery is part of test acceptance. A successful second BIOS entry is insufficient unless the approved clear removes all persistent/one-time layers, preserves the original BootOrder, permits the normal OS path and restores BMC/host health.
The source requires visual BIOS/POST evidence. API/IPMI bootparam output supplements but does not replace KVM/console observation; credentials must be protected and inline `-P` handling rejected.

ED-06 keeps warm/cold/full-power semantics distinct; this row requests node reboots and no AC/DC substitution. ED-20/ED-23 preserve visual evidence; ED-29 requires full OFF/ON/OS Ready only if a later approved power-cycle recovery is actually used, not as a silent reboot substitute.

ED-03/ED-13 permit a NOT STARTED standard BMC draft without guessed vendor semantics; ED-24 preserves the contradiction; ED-26 prohibits automatic retries; ED-33/ED-35/ED-36/ED-38 preserve source, all two-reboot/recovery coverage and the engineer-owned verdict.

test_case.test_name: Persistent BIOS Setup boot override — two-reboot proof and verified clear
test_case.purpose: After the firmware owner resolves persistent versus timed-clear flag semantics, prove that an approved BIOS/setup override survives two reboot boundaries with the required POST message, then prove every override layer is cleared and the original normal boot path recovers.
required_package: Exact node/BMC/BIOS/UEFI identity and vendor/owner mapping of persistent, one-time, valid-bit and 60-second +/-10% auto-clear semantics
Supported BIOS/setup target and set/read/clear syntax, bootparam 5 interpretation, original BootOrder/flags, exact persistent POST text or visual marker and timer-observation method

Dedicated maintenance window, explicit approval for one persistent mutation and two reboots, protected BMC credentials, KVM/console capture and independent recovery capable of clearing the override without OS access
Read-only confirmation or separately approved correction of Redfish Host Interface enabled and Network Stack disabled; BIOS exit-without-save procedure
Mandatory final clear/readback, normal BootOrder restoration, OS Ready/BMC health gates, preserved SEL/audit/kernel evidence and owner verdict
test_case.test_command: NOT STARTED. After the vendor flag-layer ruling and final approval, capture the original BootOrder/bootparam/flag/health state; verify the BIOS prerequisites without changing them; issue only the documented protected equivalent of `ipmitool chassis bootdev bios options=efiboot,persistent`; read the full relevant flag state; execute reboot 1 and reboot 2 as separate approved observations, capturing POST/KVM BIOS entry, the persistent message and flag/timer state without saving BIOS changes. Then issue the documented persistent clear equivalent of `ipmitool chassis bootdev none options=persistent`, verify every override layer cleared, restore the original BootOrder and complete one normal OS-ready/BMC-health recovery. Do not use inline credentials or run before the clear path is proven.
test_case.expected_result: The selected persistent layer matches the approved readback before each reboot, BIOS Setup and the exact persistent POST marker are independently observed on both reboot trials, the resolved 60-second behavior matches its documented layer, and no BIOS configuration is saved. The explicit clear removes all relevant override state, original BootOrder remains/restores, and the node subsequently reaches normal OS Ready with BMC health intact.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: Pending remains while flag-layer/timer semantics, POST marker or complete clear are undefined. Under the later contract, one immediate readback or one BIOS entry cannot pass two-reboot persistence; two BIOS entries cannot pass recovery unless clear/readback and normal OS boot also succeed. Wrong target, missing/ambiguous POST marker, unexpected timed clear, boot loop, saved BIOS change, failure to clear or failure to return to OS Ready is preserved for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition. The end user owns the verdict.
safety_gate: Do not set a persistent override until the exact target, flag lifetime, clear semantics and independent console recovery are verified and explicitly approved.
Do not expose BMC secrets, assume generic ipmitool syntax is supported, clear logs or infer the 60-second timer's layer from a single poll.
Do not change or save BIOS/UEFI settings while visually entering Setup; capture each reboot and POST message separately.
Stop on wrong boot target, flag mismatch, missing POST marker, unexpected timeout, loop, lost KVM/BMC/OS access or uncertain clear state; do not automatically reboot or reapply the setting.
Clear all approved override layers before closure and verify original normal boot plus OS Ready; an AC/DC cycle is not an authorized substitute.
expected_evidence: Source identity, written vendor flag/timer decision, exact BMC/BIOS version, original BootOrder/bootparam/flags, prerequisites, approvals and recovery readiness
Protected set request/result and complete readbacks before reboot 1 and reboot 2
Separate reboot timelines with KVM/console POST message, BIOS-entry visual captures, timer observations and no-save evidence
Explicit clear request/readback proving every layer removed, original BootOrder, normal OS Ready/BMC health and preserved SEL/audit/kernel evidence
No automatic retry and engineer-owned PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED decision
test_case.recovery: If the node enters an unintended target, loops, loses management, saves a BIOS change or cannot clear persistence, stop and preserve console/bootparam/BMC evidence. Use only the prevalidated independent console/PDU/vendor path to clear every documented boot-override layer and restore the captured BootOrder; do not reapply, reboot repeatedly, reset defaults or power-cycle speculatively. Escalate if normal OS Ready and BMC health cannot be proven.

source_conflict.reason: All-future/two-reboot persistence and an approximately 60-second automatic clear are competing lifecycle requirements until the platform identifies distinct flag layers or corrects the overlay semantics.

blocked.reason: The mutation, two-reboot evidence and restoration state machine are understandable; vendor lifetime mapping, exact visual marker and clear method are furnishable project prerequisites. Execution remains withheld but not irreducibly unknowable.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Persistent/one-time/timed-clear flag mapping; supported set/read/clear schema; exact POST marker; original BootOrder; two-reboot/KVM window; approval, timeout, independent recovery and normal OS-ready restoration contract.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; NO BOOT-FLAG WRITE, REBOOT, BIOS CHANGE, CLEAR, POWER OR DUT ACTION AUTHORIZED OR EXECUTED

project_authority: The BMC/BIOS firmware owner defines flag layering, timer and clear semantics; the system owner supplies the normal BootOrder and maintenance approval; the operator owns KVM/POST observation and independent recovery; the end user owns verdict. They may not waive the second reboot, visual marker or verified clear/restoration and may not modify Master in place.
